title.narrative: Policies and programmes operationalised to ensure comprehensive and sustainable social protection for all

description.narrative: Despite progress and anticipated graduation from Least Developed Country status by 2026, Bangladesh faces labour market challenges: slow job creation, low female participation, high informality (85%), poor working conditions, youth unemployment, and a large inactive working-age population (39%). In response, the government adopted the National Social Security Strategy in 2015 to promote universal life-cycle coverage. However, contribution-based social insurance remains limited, for working-age groups. ILO supported the Employment Injury Scheme (EIS), piloted in the ready-made garment sector in 2022, but broader protections for accidents, sickness, and unemployment remain absent. Existing employer-funded systems fall short of international standards. ILO’s strategy focuses on institutionalization of contributory social insurance. This begins with expanding the EIS into a national programme and using its framework to introduce protections for unemployment, maternity, and sickness. The strategy also promotes disability-inclusive policies aligned with international labour standards. Expected results include a National EIS system, an endorsed unemployment insurance scheme, improved maternity and sickness benefits, and a disability-inclusive national framework. A Social Protection Unit under the Ministry of Labour and Employment is planned to lead coordination. The ILO offers technical support for policy design, legal reform, institutional capacity building, and stakeholder engagement. It helps transition from the pilot to national insurance through actuarial studies and institutional assessments. Awareness campaigns and consultations support mainstreaming unemployment insurance. Protections for maternity, sickness, and disability are being revised in collaboration with the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics and organizations of persons with disabilities. An Assessment-Based National Dialogue will guide the next phase of the National Social Security Strategy beyond 2026.
